title: Table-Valued Functions
description: Learn how to create table-valued functions that return a table of rows.

data.text: A table-valued function is a user-defined function that returns data of a table type. The return type is a table, so you can use the function just like a table in a FROM clause.

data.title: Create inline table-valued function
data.content: Creates a function that returns products for a specific model year.
data.code:
CREATE FUNCTION udfProductInYear (
    @model_year INT
)
RETURNS TABLE
AS
RETURN
    SELECT
        product_name,
        model_year,
        list_price
    FROM
        production.products
    WHERE
        model_year = @model_year;

data.title: Use TVF in FROM clause
data.content: Calls the table-valued function like a table.

data.text: An MSTVF uses a table variable as the return value and can execute multiple statements:

data.title: Multi-statement TVF example
data.content: Combines staffs and customers into a single contact list.
data.code:
CREATE FUNCTION udfContacts()
    RETURNS @contacts TABLE (
        first_name VARCHAR(50),
        last_name VARCHAR(50),
        email VARCHAR(255),
        phone VARCHAR(25),
        contact_type VARCHAR(20)
    )
AS
BEGIN
    INSERT INTO @contacts
    SELECT first_name, last_name, email, phone, 'Staff'
    FROM sales.staffs;

    INSERT INTO @contacts
    SELECT first_name, last_name, email, phone, 'Customer'
    FROM sales.customers;

    RETURN;
END;

data.title: Table-Valued Functions Key Points
points: Table-valued functions return a table that can be used in FROM clauses.
Inline TVFs return a single SELECT statement result.
Multi-statement TVFs use a table variable and can combine multiple queries.
TVFs are more flexible than stored procedures because they can be used wherever tables are used.
